title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the 'équation des lacets' [α,ρ] = [β,σ] ε_1(ν) for sections of G = PGL_2 (more generally a group scheme G with a pair of opposite unipotent subgroups L_0, L_1, where ε_0 ∈ L_0 and ε_1 ∈ L_1). This is part of the programme of describing (non-abelian) representations of the Teichmüller groupoid π_{0,3}, π_{0,4}, π_{1,1} relevant to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller action. On the previous page a pair (ρ,σ) is encoded as a triple (l̃'_∞, l̃'_1, l̃'_0) = (ρ̃^{-1}, σ̃, ε̃_0) with product 1, so ε̃_0 = σ̃^{-1}ρ̃. The group 𝔖_3' acts on such triples by cyclic permutations and by 'inversion-reversal'.

On this page Grothendieck reads a triple as a homomorphism φ: π_{0,3} = ⟨l_0, l_1, l_∞ | l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1⟩ (a free group of rank 2) → Γ(PG), with l_i ↦ l'_i. He then identifies two operations on pairs with precomposition by outer automorphisms of π_{0,3}.

(i) The exchange (ρ,σ) ↦ (σ,ρ) is precomposition with the automorphism l_0 ↦ l_1^{-1}, l_1 ↦ l_0^{-1}. Since l_∞ = l_0^{-1} l_1^{-1}, this sends l_∞ ↦ l_1 l_0 = l_∞^{-1}. He calls it τ'_∞.

(ii) The inversion (ρ,σ) ↦ (ρ^{-1},σ^{-1}) is precomposition with l_0 ↦ l_0^{-1}, l_1 ↦ l_1^{-1}. This sends l_∞ ↦ l_0 l_1, which is conjugate to l_∞^{-1}. He calls it τ_∞ = σ_∞ τ'_∞, where σ_∞ is the orientation-preserving swap of l_0 and l_1 (l_∞ ↦ conjugate of l_∞).

Hence the four-element group of transformations of pairs (ρ,σ) introduced in §1° is the Klein subgroup ⟨τ'_∞, τ_∞⟩ ≅ Z/2 × Z/2 of Aut_ext(π_{0,3}) = 𝔖_{0,3} ≅ S_3 × Z/2 (the extended outer automorphisms, permuting the three conjugacy classes of loops up to inversion). This subgroup is the stabiliser of the third puncture/class. Therefore its effect on the third factor ε̃_0 is to keep it or replace it by its inverse, up to conjugacy. Consequently the second condition (that the third factor be a unipotent section in L_0) is automatically preserved, 'ce que nous savons'. The point is to explain conceptually the symmetries of the set of admissible (ρ,σ) in the loop equation via the dihedral/S_3×Z/2 symmetry of P^1 minus 3 points.
errors: The new triple after (ρ,σ)↦(ρ^{-1},σ^{-1}) is (ρ̃, σ̃^{-1}, x) with x = σ̃ρ̃^{-1}. With the previous page's convention ε_1 = −ρσ^{-1}, this x is ε̃_1^{-1} (in PGL_2 the sign is irrelevant), not ε̃_1 as written. In any case it is conjugate to ε̃_0^{-1}, consistent with the conclusion. This is a minor notational slip, or a matter of convention.
The transcription's l_∞ ↦ l_1 l_0 should be l_0 l_1. The two are conjugate, so the outer class is unaffected.

The text says the subgroup stabilises 'L_0 ⊂ π_{0,3}', but by the triple convention of the previous page the third factor corresponds to l_∞, the class fixed up to inversion by τ_∞ and τ'_∞. The labelling of which puncture/subgroup is meant is slightly loose but harmless.

ideas.what: Interpreting triples of group elements with product 1 as homomorphisms from π_{0,3} (free group on two generators) and symmetries as precomposition by extended outer automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: Action of Out^±(F_2) ≅ S_3 × Z/2 on character varieties / representation spaces of the thrice-punctured sphere
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Fricke–Klein; modern character variety literature, e.g. Goldman)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses π_{0,3}, the Teichmüller tower and its automorphisms, but not this computation

ideas.what: Identifying the Klein four-group of transformations of (ρ,σ) (swap, inversion) with the stabiliser of one puncture in 𝔖_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: Stabiliser of a cusp in the extended mapping class group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}

deep.surprise_reason: A routine bookkeeping step in Grothendieck's long study of the loop equation: it identifies obvious symmetries of pairs (ρ,σ) with the Klein subgroup of S_3×Z/2 = Out^±(π_{0,3}). The argument is correct up to a minor notational slip and contains nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: 'd'où l_∞ ↦ l_1 l_0[?]' should read 'd'où l_∞ ↦ l_0 l_1' (the computation gives l_0 l_1).
'sur la troisième facteur ε̃_0 = dc'_0[?]' is likely 'sur le troisième facteur ε̃_0 = l̃'_0'.
'ce qui assure la vérité de la conserver 2e condition manifestement' is likely 'ce qui assure la conservation de la 2e condition, manifestement, ce que nous savons !' (with a crossed-out word).
'Comment [-comment appliquer à ...-]': the crossed-out phrase begins a new line; the main text reads 'Comment interpréter la transformation (ρ,σ)↦(ρ^{-1},σ^{-1})'.
